hypotheses.reasoning: At 21:42:34 session-cache was replaced and came back with no RDB snapshot and 0 keys (#224). Within 30s, account-svc's cache miss ratio jumped to 98% against a 4% baseline, and it fell back to loading every session from accounts-db (#231, #235). That cache stampede pushed accounts-db to 488-496/500 connections at 94-97% CPU (#232, #240). After that, simple primary-key lookups on accounts took 3-8.7s (#243, #268), account-svc queries timed out after 5000ms (#254, #267), and edge-proxy started returning 504s on POST /login at 21:44:45. Before the restart the DB was healthy: only routine checkpoint and vacuum lines. The trigger was small (one cache node lost its data) and the damage came from the amplification (every miss hitting the database), so this is cascading_failure. Red herrings: the auth-svc IdP retry at 21:31 recovered and came well before the onset; the audit_log seq scan (#201) was a single 1.7s query; the edge-proxy disk warning and the audit-consumer GC pause are unrelated.
Another reading is that accounts-db queries simply hung and timed out. But the DB slowed down because of the load from cache misses, not because of a fault in the DB itself.
The accounts-db connections nearly ran out at 500, but that came from the stampede, not from a pool sized too small for normal load.

verdict.recommendedAction: 1. Get the session cache warm again: pre-load hot sessions, or turn on RDB/AOF persistence and replication so a replaced node doesn't come back empty. 2. Protect accounts-db from stampedes: add request coalescing (single-flight) on cache misses and rate-limit cache refills in account-svc, and temporarily shed or queue login load until the miss ratio is back near baseline. 3. Watch accounts-db connections and CPU until they settle.
